items.title: Every algebra is a directed colimit of finitely presented algebras, with surjective transitions in the finite type case
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every algebra is a directed colimit of finitely presented algebras over the base, and that in the finite type case the transition maps can be arranged to be surjective (statement lines 32054-32060). The proof gives a categorical argument and then an explicit construction indexed by finite pieces of data, and in the finite type case restricts the index set to pieces containing a fixed finite generating set so that the transitions become surjective (proof lines 32062-32094). Choosing the index set so that surjectivity comes for free is the step that settles the second assertion. H2.
